So `(\S+)\s*` works for search but not match when used alone. The issue is that `^(\S+)\s*$` requires the entire string to match, but `\s*` consumes spaces and then `$` expects end of string... oh wait, `$` should work after consuming all characters including spaces. Let me think again.

Actually, `^(\S+)\s*$` on `hello world`:
- `^` matches start
- `(\S+)` greedily matches `hello`
- `\s*` greedily matches `       ` (all spaces)
- `$` expects end of string... but we're at `world`, so it fails!

The regex engine backtracks: `\s*` gives up some spaces, but `\S+` can't extend because there's a space. So no match.

For `{<}` followed by literal like `^(\S+)\s* world$`:
- `^` matches start  
- `(\S+)` matches `hello`
- `\s*` matches `       ` (all spaces)
- ` world` matches ` world` ✓
- `$` matches end ✓

OK so the pattern works for the case with trailing content but not standalone.

One solution: use `(?:\s|$)` instead of `\s*`. But as I tested earlier, this breaks the case with trailing content because it stops too early.

Alternative: use `(?:\s*\b|\s*$)` or something... too complex.

Another idea: change the pattern to `(\S+)(?=\s|$)` - lookahead instead of consuming. But then we don't consume the whitespace for alignment purposes.
